verdict.rationale: Docs show sessions are persisted to disk and can be resumed later, and a hosting guide covers subprocess architecture, session persistence, scaling, and multi-tenant isolation for Docker/Kubernetes deployments — supporting some durability across restarts. However there is no mention of integration with durable-execution frameworks (e.g., Temporal, Restate) or explicit guarantees of resuming long-running agent state across process crashes/deploys beyond session-file replay. Missing for 10: durable-execution engine integrations, documented crash/restart recovery semantics beyond simple session resume, and independent verification of production durability at scale.
